grammar_rules.summary: Use the infinitive as stem and add endings -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont. For -re verbs, drop the e before adding endings.
grammar_rules.explanation: To form the futur simple of most verbs, use the infinitive as the stem and add the endings -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont. For -re verbs, drop the e from the infinitive before adding the endings.
common_traps: dropping the final e for -re verbs

attestations.source_text: To form the futur simple of most verbs, use the infinitive as the stem and add the endings -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont. For -re verbs, drop the e from the infinitive before adding the endings.

grammar_rules.summary: Some irregular verbs have irregular stems in the future tense; the endings remain the same.
grammar_rules.explanation: The endings of the futur simple are the same for all verbs. However, some irregular verbs have irregular stems. You simply have to memorize them.
common_traps: confusing irregular stems with regular infinitive stems

attestations.source_text: However, some irregular verbs have irregular stems. You simply have to memorize them.

grammar_rules.summary: Some verbs have slight spelling modifications in the future stem (e.g., acheter -> j'achèterai, appeler -> j'appellerai, employer -> j'emploierai).
grammar_rules.explanation: Some slight spelling modifications occur with some verbs. These are seen throughout all persons of the future conjugation.

attestations.source_text: Some slight spelling modifications occur with some verbs.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Use of futur simple for future events
grammar_rules.summary: The futur simple describes future events, as in English.
grammar_rules.explanation: As in English, the French future tense is used to describe future events.
usage: to describe future actions or states

attestations.source_text: As in English, the French future tense is used to describe future events.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Future in both clauses after certain conjunctions
grammar_rules.summary: After conjunctions like quand, lorsque, dès que, aussitôt que, tant que, both main and dependent clauses use futur simple when referring to future.
grammar_rules.explanation: In a compound sentence in French, if the main clause is in the futur simple, the dependent clause, introduced by some conjunctions, will also be in the futur simple. Note that in English, such a dependent clause will be in the present tense.
grammar_rules.formation: main clause futur simple + conjunction + dependent clause futur simple
usage: to express future actions in temporal clauses
conditions: conjunctions: aussitôt que, dès que, lorsque, quand, tant que
common_traps: using present tense in French dependent clause after these conjunctions (as in English)

attestations.source_text: In a compound sentence in French, if the main clause is in the futur simple, the dependent clause, introduced by some conjunctions, will also be in the futur simple.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Futur simple for probability in present
grammar_rules.summary: The futur simple of être and avoir can express probability or likelihood in the present.
grammar_rules.explanation: The future tense of être and avoir is sometimes used to express probability in the present, to indicate something that is likely or allegedly true.
usage: to express probability or supposition about present
common_traps: not using future of être/avoir when expressing probability about present

attestations.source_text: The future tense of être and avoir is sometimes used to express probability in the present.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Futur simple in narration (future from past standpoint)
grammar_rules.summary: In narration, futur simple can express a future idea from the standpoint of the past; English uses 'would'.
grammar_rules.explanation: In a narration, the futur simple can be used to express a future idea from the standpoint of the past. Note that English uses a conditional form, would, in this case.
usage: in historical or literary narration to express future relative to past
common_traps: using conditional in French instead of futur simple in this context

attestations.source_text: In a narration, the futur simple can be used to express a future idea from the standpoint of the past.

grammar_rules.summary: Futur simple can replace imperative for a less peremptory tone.
grammar_rules.explanation: The futur simple can be used instead of an imperative (command form) to achieve a less peremptory tone.
usage: to make polite requests or soften commands
common_traps: using imperative when a softer tone is intended

attestations.source_text: The futur simple can be used instead of an imperative (command form) to achieve a less peremptory tone.

grammar_rules.summary: Use future tense of avoir or être + past participle of main verb; agreement same as passé composé.
grammar_rules.explanation: The futur antérieur describes an action that will take place and be completed before another future action. To form this compound tense, use the future tense of avoir or être + the past participle of the main verb. Agreement rules are the same as for the passé composé.
grammar_rules.formation: futur simple of auxiliary (avoir/être) + past participle
usage: to express an action completed before a future time or action
restrictions: auxiliary choice depends on verb (avoir or être)
exceptions: verbs using être require agreement with subject
agreement_rules: past participle agrees with subject when auxiliary is être; with avoir, agrees with preceding direct object

attestations.source_text: The futur antérieur describes an action that will take place and be completed before another future action. To form this compound tense, use the future tense of avoir or être + the past participle of the main verb.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Use of futur antérieur for completed future action
grammar_rules.summary: Futur antérieur expresses an action that will be completed before another future action.
grammar_rules.explanation: The futur antérieur describes an action that will take place and be completed before another future action.
usage: to express completion before a future point
common_traps: using futur simple when anteriority is intended

attestations.source_text: The futur antérieur describes an action that will take place and be completed before another future action.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Choice between futur simple and futur antérieur in dependent clauses
grammar_rules.summary: When both clauses use futur simple, actions are simultaneous; use futur antérieur in dependent clause to mark anteriority.
grammar_rules.explanation: Sometimes you have a choice between the futur simple and the futur antérieur. When both clauses use the futur simple, it is implied that both actions take place simultaneously. If you want to mark an anteriority, use the futur antérieur.
grammar_rules.formation: main clause futur simple + conjunction + (futur simple for simultaneous / futur antérieur for anterior)
usage: to indicate simultaneity or anteriority in future temporal clauses
conditions: after conjunctions like quand, lorsque, dès que, aussitôt que, tant que
common_traps: using futur simple when anteriority is intended

attestations.source_text: Sometimes you have a choice between the futur simple and the futur antérieur. When both clauses use the futur simple, it is implied that both actions take place simultaneously. If you want to mark an anteriority, use the futur antérieur.

grammar_rules.rule_name: Futur antérieur for probability of past action
grammar_rules.summary: Futur antérieur can express probability of a past action, analogous to futur simple for present probability.
grammar_rules.explanation: The futur antérieur can also express the probability of a past action, in the same way that the futur simple can be used to express probability in the present.
usage: to express supposition about a past event

attestations.source_text: The futur antérieur can also express the probability of a past action, in the same way that the futur simple can be used to express probability in the present.

grammar_rules.summary: Futur antérieur is used after 'si' when it means 'whether', implying a completed action.
grammar_rules.explanation: The futur antérieur is also used after si, implying a completed action. Si means whether in this case.
usage: to express uncertainty about a completed future action
restrictions: only when 'si' means 'whether', not 'if' for condition
common_traps: using futur simple or present after 'si' when 'si' means 'whether'

attestations.source_text: The futur antérieur is also used after si, implying a completed action. Si means whether in this case.

grammar_rules.rule_name: No futur simple after 'si' in future condition
grammar_rules.summary: In French, futur simple is never used after 'si' implying a future condition; present tense is used instead.
grammar_rules.explanation: In French, the futur antérieur is never used after si implying a future condition. Use the present instead. (Note: this also applies to futur simple.)
grammar_rules.formation: si + present tense, main clause futur simple/imperative
usage: to express a condition for a future action
restrictions: only when 'si' means 'if' introducing a condition
common_traps: using future tense after 'si' in conditional sentences

attestations.source_text: In French, the futur antérieur is never used after si implying a future condition. Use the present instead.

grammar_rules.summary: List of conjunctions that require indicative mood, including those seen with future and additional ones.
grammar_rules.explanation: Let's learn a few more conjunctions followed by the indicative mood. These include: alors que, après que, comme, étant donné que, maintenant que, parce que, pendant que, puisque, si, sous prétexte que, tandis que, vu que.
usage: to introduce subordinate clauses with indicative
common_traps: using subjunctive after these conjunctions (subjunctive is used with other conjunctions in Chapter 13)

exceptions_and_traps.title: Futur simple vs futur antérieur in dependent clauses
exceptions_and_traps.description: When both clauses are in futur simple, actions are simultaneous. To mark anteriority, use futur antérieur in the dependent clause.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Elle vous téléphonera dès qu'elle aura fini son roman.
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: Elle vous téléphonera dès qu'elle finira son roman. (if anteriority intended)

attestations.source_text: Sometimes you have a choice between the futur simple and the futur antérieur. When both clauses use the futur simple, it is implied that both actions take place simultaneously. If you want to mark an anteriority, use the futur antérieur.

exceptions_and_traps.title: No future tense after 'si' in future condition
exceptions_and_traps.description: In French, neither futur simple nor futur antérieur is used after 'si' when it means 'if' introducing a future condition. Use present tense instead.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: S'il a le temps, il passera vous voir.
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: S'il aura le temps, il passera vous voir.

attestations.source_text: In French, the futur antérieur is never used after si implying a future condition. Use the present instead.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Futur antérieur after 'si' meaning 'whether'
exceptions_and_traps.description: After 'si' meaning 'whether', futur antérieur can be used to imply a completed action. This is different from 'si' meaning 'if'.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Je me demande s'ils auront signé le contrat.
exceptions_and_traps.incorrect_form: Je me demande s'ils signeront le contrat.

attestations.source_text: The futur antérieur is also used after si, implying a completed action. Si means whether in this case.

exceptions_and_traps.title: Future tenses for probability
exceptions_and_traps.description: Futur simple expresses probability in present; futur antérieur expresses probability of past.
exceptions_and_traps.correct_form: Il sera distrait. (present probability) / Il aura encore brûlé le gigot. (past probability)

attestations.source_text: The future tense of être and avoir is sometimes used to express probability in the present. / The futur antérieur can also express the probability of a past action.
